# Release Notes v0.7.1

**Released:** 2026-10-20

This release lands GPU-resident multi-zone scenes (Spec 86), an effect livecoding loop that agents and the CLI can drive end to end, and a daemon-wide error envelope for every HTTP extractor rejection. Alongside those, the persistence layer gained a stated durability contract with a verified skip path, and the WebSocket protocol gained a microsecond publication clock.

## 🌟 Highlights

### ✨ GPU-resident multi-zone scenes
A scene with more than one LED zone used to lose GPU residency unless every layout sampled Nearest with Clamp. Zones fell back to CPU canvases, collided on a single compositor-wide readback latch keyed only by size, and came back black; the render loop dropped to the 10 fps minimal tier and `GET /api/v1/canvas/frame` returned black images. Every zone now retains its own `GpuProjectionSnapshot` texture and is sampled through `LedSamplingStrategy::SparkleFlingerZones`, a concatenated dispatch with one params uniform per pass and one readback of per-zone LED colors. Gaussian-area plans now sample on the GPU with CPU-exact fixed-point arithmetic, so no sampling mode forces a fallback.

### 🤖 Effect livecoding loop
`install_effect`, `get_effect_console`, and `capture_canvas` join the MCP tool set (21 total), with matching `hypercolor effects install`, `effects console`, and `effects capture` CLI subcommands and `POST /api/v1/effects/install`, `GET /api/v1/effects/console`, `GET /api/v1/canvas/frame` routes. The effect console journal keeps 512 entries with monotonic sequence numbers and remaps runtime-copy line numbers back to the author's file through `RuntimeLineShift`, so a stack trace points at the source you edited. `install_effect` returns a `console_after` cursor taken before the page loads, so the next console read covers exactly that version's output. The `skills/effect-livecoding` skill documents the install, apply, read console, capture loop.

### 🐛 Every extractor rejection renders the error envelope
A malformed body, an undecodable path segment, or a bad typed query value used to escape Axum's stock extractors as a bare text/plain reply. `crates/hypercolor-daemon/src/api/extract.rs` adds `ApiJson`, `ApiPath`, `ApiQuery`, `ApiMultipart`, `ApiRequestExtension`, and `ApiWebSocketUpgrade`, each rendering the canonical envelope with a stable code, the decoder's diagnostic, and a `details.field` path from `serde_path_to_error`. Broken JSON answers `400 malformed_request`, a wrong shape answers `422 validation_error`, an oversized body answers `413 payload_too_large` without naming a limit Axum does not expose, and a missing request extension answers `500 internal_error` with the diagnostic kept in the log rather than sent to the client.

### ⚡️ Scene commits stop paying for durable work they already did
A live control PATCH measured 42.7 ms p50 server-side (face PUT 46.5 ms, effect apply 61.3 ms), partly because each commit rewrote `driver-inventory.json` twice and re-persisted `scenes.json` right after the commit. The persistence layer now records a SHA-256 of the bytes it last made durable per destination alongside a platform change stamp (device, inode, ctime on Unix; volume serial, file ID, ChangeTime on Windows) and skips a write whose bytes are already on disk. Scene commit file I/O moved to the blocking pool, and each WebSocket session runs its commands on a dedicated lane so a slow PATCH no longer stalls the session's outbound queues into `resync_required`.

### 🔧 Microsecond publication clock on the WebSocket
`event`, `metrics`, `device_metrics`, and `sensors` now carry `timestamp` and `mono_us`; `hello` carries `clock_epoch` and `mono_us`; command responses carry an optional `mono_us` stamped inside the round trip at the socket handoff. Clients can order messages within one daemon run, measure intervals at microsecond resolution, bound clock offset from a round trip, and spot a restart by comparing `clock_epoch`. The protocol deliberately does not promise `mono_us` a steady rate: it reads `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` and follows NTP frequency corrections, so long sessions must recalibrate.

## 🎨 Rendering and Studio

- Per-zone observability on every frame: `gpu_sampled_zone_count`, `cpu_sampled_zone_count`, `held_zone_count`, `gpu_sampling_passes`, and `zone_composition_skips` flow from frame metrics through the slow-frame log, pacing window, WebSocket timeline, REST status, and the diagnose snapshot. All default to zero so older payloads still decode.
- A new `multi_zone_sampling` diagnose check warns when a multi-zone frame holds a zone that had no frame to sample.
- Transitions into and out of multi-zone scenes blend in LED space, so overlapping LEDs no longer fade from the wrong zone's color. A single-zone incoming scene samples its own pre-crossfade frame as a one-zone set, captured only during a transition.
- Both render compositors now open one wgpu device. Previously, with `render_gpu_device` unset, the display compositor opened its own and read black.
- Each render frame bounds the GPU work it may leave queued and ends that work on every path, early exits included; staging buffers are freed on every submission.
- Zones skip recomposition when their composition key matches the held snapshot, and an unchanged media canvas uploads into its texture once.
- Studio zone previews are published for GPU-resident zones, queued behind LED work. Saved primary-zone placements stay in the active layout, and a Save carries only what it changed into the shared layout.
- Display faces are paced on a due-time cadence, and Servo keeps WebGL drawing buffers between frame captures.

## 🔌 Devices and discovery

- A device that refuses a frame is now its own outcome: `DeviceWriteOutcome::Declined` and `DeviceDeliveryStatus::Declined`, counted as `transport_declined` separately from `frames_sent`, `transport_failed`, and `errors_total`. A decline does not extend a failure streak or force a reconnect. `/diagnose` reports `transport_declined` per device output.
- Binary frame acks accept only `0x01` and `0x00`; any other byte now drops the connection instead of being read as a decline.
- A new blocks watcher (`crates/hypercolor-core/src/device/blocks/watcher.rs`) subscribes to blocksd device events and requests a driver-scoped scan on add or remove, coalescing arrivals in a 150 ms window.
- Drivers can call `request_discovery(driver_id)` to trigger a scan without waiting for the periodic interval. Scans run per target in their own lanes (`crates/hypercolor-daemon/src/discovery/lanes.rs`), so one failing scanner no longer suppresses another target's departures, and every scan task drains before shutdown cleanup.
- Background connects carry a fence checked against the lane's observation epoch, so a stale connect cannot resurrect a device a newer scan retired.
- Display zones orphaned by the move to driver-scoped fingerprints are remapped from their pre-scoping id, colliding zones are collapsed (the one with layers wins; otherwise the newer layer id), and the migration publishes `ZoneChanged` and `SceneLibraryChanged` so clients refresh instead of holding stale targets.

## ⚡️ Aura SMBus throughput

Every SMBus batch took one process-wide exclusive lock per bus and held it through its in-batch 1 ms delays, so two Aura DIMMs on one i801 bus fully serialized. **Measured before the change: sticks targeting 60 fps landed near 19 fps with `avg_write_ms` around 50.** Three changes remove the serialization and the bus traffic behind that ceiling (no post-change frame rate was measured):

- The arbiter hands out two kinds of claim. A bus claim stays exclusive; a device claim takes the bus shared plus a lock for its own address, so transactions to different ENE chips interleave on the wire while one address still sees one writer at a time. Probes, hub remaps, and every read keep the whole bus; Windows keeps bus claims throughout.
- The Aura encoder emits pairs only for LEDs a frame changes, latching only when something went out, with a full write every 60th frame and after any failed, unreported, or post-reconnect frame. Frames that encode nothing report as `SuppressedDuplicate` so `avg_write_ms` stays true to real writes.
- DRAM direct mode (register `0x8020`) is asserted only when the DIMM's colors are unknown, removing two SMBus transactions and a 1 ms delay from every steady-state DRAM frame.

## 💾 Durability contract

- A write reporting `Written` or `DurableWritten` leaves the destination durably holding its payload with the requested mode, covering the destination's own directory entry in its parent. Ancestors above the parent are out of scope, as is a writer still active during the call.
- A skip is never taken on a matching stamp alone. The destination is reopened without following a final symlink (`O_NOFOLLOW` on Unix, `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` on Windows), confirmed to be a regular file opened non-blocking so a FIFO cannot stall a pool thread, checked for the requested mode, byte-verified, then synced along with the parent directory entry.
- The requested mode is applied before the staged file is synced, so bytes and mode become durable together. An explicit `0o000` is now a real request rather than a sentinel for "no request".
- One directory barrier runs per durable write instead of two.
- The scene service tracks the newest store revision its own receipts cover and skips the per-commit store save with no I/O while they do, still verifying on whole-session saves at shutdown, power events, and device removal. On btrfs, an fsync of a 461 KB `scenes.json` measured p50 3.25 ms, p90 7.6 ms, max 90 ms.

## 🛠️ API, config, and tooling

- `crates/hypercolor-daemon/clippy.toml` disallows `axum::Json`, `axum::Form`, `axum::Extension`, `axum::extract::Path`, `axum::extract::Query`, `axum::extract::Multipart`, and `axum::extract::ws::WebSocketUpgrade` outside `api::extract`: the six wrapped families plus `Form`, which no handler takes. The file notes its own limits, reading spelled types rather than inferred closure patterns and not covering `Bytes`, `String`, `RawForm`, `RawPathParams`, `NestedPath`, or `MatchedPath`. The `api_rejection_sweep_tests` suite closes the behavioral side for documented operations, probing 315 cases across 46 JSON bodies, ~20 multipart bodies, 69 path parameters, and 22 typed query parameters.
- Multipart upload request bodies are documented in OpenAPI, with optional upload parts modeled as absent rather than null, and the canvas route documents both media types it returns.
- Authoritative config documents decode strictly through `HypercolorConfig::deserialize_strict`: an unknown key in `hypercolor.toml`, a CLI or env overlay, or a REST config write is refused by dotted path (`unknown config keys daemon.prot`) instead of vanishing. Client-side decoding went the other way, dropping `deny_unknown_fields` from every config section so an older UI can read a newer daemon's payload.
- Build and supply chain: rustls moved to 0.23.46 for four RustSec advisories, `utoipa-swagger-ui` 10.0.1 is vendored unmodified and built against zip 9, and the cargo cache wrapper prunes idle incremental directories before Cargo starts, keeping prune trash inside each profile and surfacing it in `just disk`.
- New specs: `docs/specs/85-show-grade-cuts.md` (zone cues and show-grade cuts, phase one ready) and `docs/specs/86-gpu-resident-multi-zone.md` (phase one closed in code).

## 💥 Breaking changes

- **Config schema 6.** `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is now 6; the config store reads schemas 4 through 6 and writes 6. Once a file is saved at schema 6, builds that read only up to schema 5 refuse it.
- **Beat detection default raised from 0.6 to 1.2.** `audio.beat_sensitivity` keeps its name but behaves as a threshold: higher triggers only on stronger hits. The schema 6 migration removes an explicit `0.6` (within 1e-6) so the new default applies; any other value you set is kept. On a synthetic five-genre corpus at -6 and -15 dBFS, beats landing on neither kick nor snare fell from 11.0/s to 3.8/s while kick recall went from 99.3% to 93.0%. It still fires on some hats and bright hits, and can fire 35-150 ms after a kick. The Studio slider is relabeled **Beat Threshold**.
- **Unknown config keys are now fatal** for files, overlays, and REST config writes. A typo that previously vanished silently now fails the load with its dotted path.
- **WebSocket manifest schema 3.** The manifest gained a top-level `clock` block. Tooling pinned to schema 2 needs updating.
- **Malformed-request replies changed shape.** Clients that parsed Axum's plain-text rejection strings now receive the JSON error envelope with a stable code; parse `error.code` rather than the message.

## 📝 Upgrade notes

- Configs on schema 4 and 5 migrate automatically on load; anything older is refused. For a schema 3 or earlier file, follow the refusal message: set `schema_version = 4` by hand (not 6, which would skip the v4 and v5 steps) and, if the file predates the interaction-route split, add `daemon_route = "merge"` and `preview_route = "browser"` under `[input]`. The daemon upgrades the edited file the rest of the way on load.
- If you relied on the old 0.6 beat behavior, set `audio.beat_sensitivity` explicitly before upgrading; the migration preserves any value other than 0.6.
- Validate your `hypercolor.toml` against the strict decode before rolling out. Keys that silently did nothing will now stop the daemon from starting, and the error names the exact path.
- Regenerate or update API clients: the Python client gained `canvas` and effect console models, `mono_us` and `clock_epoch` fields (all optional, `None` against older daemons), and `transport_declined` on diagnose output.
- CI running GPU tests should use the WARP lane, which now covers zone rendering, composer, and render-thread integration tests. The preview cadence test stays excluded because WARP says nothing about delivered frame rate on real hardware.
